answer: As a ridge shelters a harbor from an ocean gale, stake-weighted voting shields an agent marketplace from floods of fake identities. Each agent must lock tokens in escrow, and its voting power equals its deposited stake, not its number of accounts. Splitting one deposit across a thousand identities buys no extra influence. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up costly capital.
